decisions.reason: As a newly launched line close to the core range, it is likely to be retained because a large firm in a growing market has enough slack to give it more time unless results clearly fall below aspiration levels.
This handle family fits the established business and system-breadth strategy, so management would usually keep it while learning about demand rather than redeploy resources immediately.
A single new design variant faces some pruning risk if it underperforms peer and internal aspirations, but the short time on the market and close fit with the core offer favor retention.
Like other recent core-range design introductions, it would normally be kept for another period because performance is still uncertain and the firm can absorb modest shortfalls.
This product family supports the firm's broad portfolio across project needs, making withdrawal unlikely absent clear evidence of persistent underperformance.
